summary: External recurrent checkpoint restores can reserve execution capacity and retain ownership through admission.
compatibility: Use with the paired LMCache restore-admission change to wait for checkpoint capacity instead of recomputing cached prefixes.
details: Restores reserve GPU blocks and running slots before copies start, and keep restored pages owned until execution takes over.
Sliding-window and chunked-local continuation reservations count physical pages rather than skipped positions in the block table.
Requests with reserved capacity can progress past a blocked queue head; cancellation releases reservations after submitted copies drain.
Existing external-checkpoint callers retain their previous behavior unless they opt into admission reservations.
